summary: John Ross Carter worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith (~1966–1972). He served as a professor at Colgate University's Chapel House (~1972–2006).

John S. Strong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin, Hartford Seminary, and the University of Chicago under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Frank E. Reynolds. He taught at Bates College (1987–1988).

John Sampson worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Liverpool and the University of Oxford, and he served as University Librarian at the University of Liverpool from 1892 to 1928.

John Scudder Chandler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Yale University (B.A. ~1866–1870). He served as acting principal of Pasumalai Seminary (1890–1892), Fellow at the University of Madras (1913–1922), and director of Kodaikanal Language School (1924–1928).

John Shakespear specialized in linguistics and Indology. Educated at Wellington College and the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst under John Richardson, he served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Sandhurst (1805–1809) and Professor of Hindustani at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).
John Shore was an Indology and history scholar who succeeded William Jones and served as President of The Asiatic Society in 1794.

John Shortt was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Madras Medical College and the University of Aberdeen (M.D. 1850). He worked for the East India Company (~1846) and served as Assistant Surgeon at the University of Madras (1854–1878).

John Sinclair Stevenson was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Clifton College, Lincoln College, the University of Edinburgh, and Princeton Theological Seminary. He served as a missionary with the Presbyterian Church in Ireland from 1894 to 1924.
John Snelling was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as General Secretary of the Buddhist Society (~1980–1984) and editor of The Middle Way (~1980–1988).

John Stevenson was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served as a missionary (~1823–1834), East India Company chaplain (1834–1854), and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1855–1858).

John Stirling Morley Hooper was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Oxford (~1901–1905). He served as Headmaster of Wesley Higher Secondary School (1930) and General Secretary of the Bible Society of India (1941).

John Strachan was a linguist who studied at Aberdeen, Cambridge, and Jena under Berthold Delbrück and Rudolf Thurneysen. He was a Fellow at Pembroke College, Cambridge, and served as Professor of Greek (1885) and Sanskrit (1889) at Owens College.

John Stratton Hawley is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Amherst College and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught at Bowdoin College (~1974–1977) before becoming Claire Tow Professor of Religion at Columbia University (~1986).
John Stuart Mill worked in philosophy and history. He studied at University College London and held a post at the East India Company from ~1823 to 1858.

John Sydenham Furnivall was a history scholar who studied at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, and Leiden University. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910 and held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1936–1942).

John Taber is an Indologist and philosopher who completed his doctorate at the University of Hamburg (1973–1979) under Lambert Schmithausen and Reiner Wiehl. He taught at Case Western Reserve University (~1982–1989) and the University of New Mexico (~1989).
John Taylor was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He earned an M.D. from the University of Edinburgh in 1804 and served with the London Missionary Society from 1805 to 1807.

John Thayer Hitchcock worked in Indology and related fields. He studied at Amherst, Chicago, Connecticut, and Cornell, and he held faculty positions at UC Berkeley (1957–1958), UCLA (1958–1966), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1966–1982).

John Thompson Platts was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bedford School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held teaching and leadership posts at Benares College and Saugor High School before becoming Teacher of Persian at the University of Oxford in 1880.

John Van Someren Pope was an Indologist and linguist who earned his M.A. at the University of Cambridge (~1867–1871). He was a professor at Presidency University and became Reader in Modern East Indian Languages at Trinity College Dublin in 1913.
